findings.citation: `python -m taste_engine.eval.benchmark` (run from `apps/taste-engine` with `PYTHONPATH=src`) runs `run_benchmark` on `eval/fixtures/household.json` and writes the result as JSON to `eval/reports/ml-01-baselines.json`.
findings.description: The verifier calls run_benchmark and reads the committed report separately, but never invokes the module entry point, so a broken or non-reproducible main/report-writing path can pass.

findings.citation: The code must use only the Python 3.12 standard library.
findings.description: No check inspects imports or dependency usage; in particular, non-standard-library use in an unexecuted path such as main is not detected.

findings.citation: "Latest event" for a (viewer, title) pair means the event with the greatest `ts`; if two events share a `ts`, the one later in the input list wins.
findings.description: The split and ranking probes do not isolate a same-viewer, same-title, equal-timestamp pair with conflicting ratings, so the input-order tie rule is not verified.

findings.citation: Score = cosine(profile, title embedding), `0.0` if either vector has zero norm, rounded with `round(score, 9)`.
findings.description: The rank probes assert ordinary held-out rankings but contain no focused zero-norm profile or zero-norm title case, so this mandated fallback can be omitted while retaining the checked rankings.

findings.citation: Paired comparison on per-viewer NDCG@10, `d = ndcg_a − ndcg_b`: a win for A if `d > 1e-12`, a win for B if `d < −1e-12`, otherwise a tie.
findings.description: The comparison probes cover exact ties and materially different scores, not differences near the 1e-12 boundary; exact comparison without the required tolerance can pass.

publicationScope: Admission judgments and native outcome metadata only; prompts, raw streams, HTTP bodies, configuration and credential state excluded.
